articleBlocks: Marble and Granite can make this board feel like countertops or building materials at first. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Sandstone gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.

solutionNarrative: Marble, Slate, and Granite first pulled me toward construction or design materials, which is why the board felt broader than it really was. That read was not wrong in everyday language, but it was too surface-level for a clean Pinpoint solve.

Sandstone corrected that. It pointed back to geology, and once I followed that cue, Marble, Obsidian, Slate, and Granite all read as rock names first rather than as finished products or decor materials.
